framework.title: BRACE and the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications

mappings.name: Agent Goal Hijack
mappings.rationale: BRACE assumes some injections will work. R02 tests that a hijacked goal still can't cause harm, and B05 and B06 stop destructive actions without approval. It can't stop the model from being steered in the first place.

mappings.name: Tool Misuse and Exploitation
mappings.rationale: The harness allows only needed tools and arguments, sets budgets, and blocks destructive calls. The gateway enforces the same rules at the boundary. R09 catches misuse spread across allowed steps.

mappings.name: Identity and Privilege Abuse
mappings.rationale: Each agent has its own identity and short-lived, narrow tokens. E08 stops delegated authority from growing as it passes between agents. B04 can cut off the agent without cutting off its user.

mappings.name: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
mappings.rationale: Dependencies, images, models, and tools are vetted, pinned, and listed in the release manifest. Tools are re-checked each time they load, so a changed tool is caught.

mappings.name: Unexpected Code Execution (RCE)
mappings.rationale: Code runs in a minimal, isolated runtime, with a stronger sandbox for untrusted code. Network limits keep a breakout from reaching much. BRACE does not find bugs in the code itself.

mappings.name: Memory & Context Poisoning
mappings.rationale: Memory is split by tenant and agent, writes are checked, and each entry records where it came from. R05 and R06 are Detection items, required only at higher stakes. Checks on writes can't spot every poisoned fact.

mappings.name: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
mappings.rationale: Messages from peer agents are treated as untrusted and sent through an authenticating gateway, and the audit trail follows calls across services. BRACE does not set a message protocol, encryption, or replay rules.

mappings.name: Cascading Failures
mappings.rationale: Budgets cap runaway work, and a tested kill switch stops an agent and all its sub-agents in a safe state. Fleet response and rollback limit spread. BRACE does not test how errors flow through a whole multi-agent system.

mappings.name: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation
mappings.rationale: Approvals show the reviewer the exact action, so a persuasive summary can't hide it. BRACE does not measure over-trust, social engineering of users, or how the agent presents itself.

mappings.name: Rogue Agents
mappings.rationale: BRACE watches for misaligned behavior and drift, and can stop a rogue agent and its sub-agents. Isolation and least privilege limit the damage. R08–R10 are Detection items, and no check proves an agent is aligned.
